# AETHER synthetic benchmark

Generated by `make gate5-reports` from `reports/experiments/results/`.

> **Evidence class: SYNTHETIC experiment.** AETHER Field is fictional. This telemetry comes from an uncalibrated, simplified model, not a validated engineering simulator, so these results say nothing about detection on any real gas system.

## Dataset

272 cases of 7 days at 300 s sampling, generated under the process guard with outcomes {'OK': 272}. Dataset SHA-256 `52e38b27fbea6443...`.

| Split | Cases |
|---|---:|
| held_out | 112 |
| test | 32 |
| train | 96 |
| validation | 32 |

Every case varies well deliverability, sensor noise, compressor capacity, and a stepped suction setpoint, which is normal operating variation no detector is told about. Fault cases vary severity, onset, and ramp. Planned well shut-ins and communication dropouts are normal operation, not anomalies. Seeds and parameter sets never repeat across splits, and fault truth is stored apart from telemetry.

Held-out regimes, never used in fitting or threshold setting: higher and lower severity, unseen assets (GS-TRUNK, C-03 and C-04, Pad B sensors), noise 2 to 3 times higher, deliverability outside the training band, onset earlier or later than in training, compressor setpoints outside training with one unit offline, and faults with an overlapping dropout. Setpoint steps of 2% can reach just inside the training range's edge.

## In-regime test

Same parameter ranges as training, with new seeds and parameters.

| Gradient boosting | 10 of 20 | 0.500 | 0.000 | 0.500 (0.267 to 0.714) | 0.000 (0.000 to 0.000) | 0.000 | 0 |

## The six Gate 4 scenarios

The accepted Gate 4 runs, unchanged, scored by the same models. One seed and fixed parameters, so this is a reference, not an estimate.

| `AETHER-NET-COMM-DROPOUT` | COMMUNICATION_FAULT | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) |
| `AETHER-NET-COMPRESSOR-DERATE` | PHYSICAL_FAULT | detected at 15.3 h, 0 before onset | detected at 0.2 h, 0 before onset | detected at 0.2 h, 0 before onset | missed, 0 before onset | detected at 0.2 h, 0 before onset |
| `AETHER-NET-NORMAL` | NORMAL | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) | 0 alarm(s) |
| `AETHER-NET-PLANNED-SHUTDOWN` | PLANNED_OPERATION | 2 alarm(s) | 2 alarm(s) | 1 alarm(s) | 4 alarm(s) | 2 alarm(s) |
| `AETHER-NET-SENSOR-DRIFT` | SENSOR_FAULT | missed, 0 before onset | detected at 25.0 h, 0 before onset | detected at 24.2 h, 0 before onset | missed, 0 before onset | missed, 0 before onset |

## Limits

- The simulator is uncalibrated and quasi-steady, so the benchmark rewards detecting this model's behavior.
- A linear model fitting this well partly reflects that the simulator is smooth and its faults have consistent signatures.
- Per-category counts are small: 4 events each in-regime, and 2 per category in each held-out regime.

# Model comparison

Generated by `make gate5-reports` from `reports/experiments/results/`.

> **Two evidence classes, never pooled.** 3W results are OBSERVED benchmark evidence from recorded offshore data. AETHER results are SYNTHETIC experiments on a fictional, uncalibrated model. Neither establishes field-validated detection performance.

All methods use the same splits, the same causal features, preprocessing fitted on training data only, and the same operating point. Parameters were fixed in advance and not tuned. Selection follows the declared rule: within both alarm limits, the false-alarm budget, best event skill, then the simplest tied method.

## Selection

| Track | Data used | Preferred | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3W (OBSERVED) | Development wells | Static limits | 1 method(s) met both alarm limits. static_threshold had the best event skill among them (-0.001). 1 method(s) have skill intervals including it, and static_threshold is the simplest of them. |
| AETHER (SYNTHETIC) | In-regime test | Gradient boosting | 1 method(s) met both alarm limits. hist_gradient_boosting had the best event skill among them (0.500). 1 method(s) have skill intervals including it, and hist_gradient_boosting is the simplest of them. |

## Tradeoffs

| Method | 3W development skill | 3W holdout skill | AETHER in-regime skill | AETHER held-out skill | 3W development false alarms per hour | Explainability | Maintainability | p95 window latency, 3W / AETHER (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Static limits | -0.001 | 0.025 | 0.379 | -0.021 | 0.002 | High: one fixed band per sensor | Low: fixed limits, refit only to recompute bands | 0.15 / 0.06 |
| Rolling deviation | 0.127 | 0.042 | 0.286 | 0.222 | 0.067 | High: names the sensor that moved from its own past | Low: no training labels | 0.84 / 1.23 |
| Logistic regression | 0.156 | 0.200 | 0.567 | 0.179 | 0.013 | Medium: linear weights on named features | Medium: retrain when sensors change | 0.41 / 0.46 |
| Isolation forest | -0.096 | 0.033 | -0.014 | -0.023 | 0.035 | Low: path-length score with no direct reason | Medium: retrain on fresh normal data | 4.24 / 4.12 |
| Gradient boosting | -0.051 | -0.067 | 0.500 | 0.329 | 0.019 | Low: 150 trees | Higher: retrain and recheck calibration | 4.17 / 1.73 |

Explainability and maintainability are judgments about each method's form, not measurements. Robustness is in [robustness](robustness.md), and latency in [inference performance](inference_performance.md).

## Reading the two tracks together

The tracks answer different questions and are never averaged. A method winning on AETHER shows it can detect this simulator's faults. Only the 3W results bear on recorded industrial data, and only for offshore oil wells at a fixed operating point without per-well adaptation.

# 3W benchmark

Generated by `make gate5-reports` from `reports/experiments/results/`.

> **Evidence class: OBSERVED benchmark.** Petrobras 3W is recorded offshore oil-well data, labeled by its publisher. It is an independent benchmark and was never measured at AETHER Field. It covers a deterministic 498-instance subset of 3W 2.0.0, and these results don't establish field-validated detection performance.

## Design

- **Data:** the 299 real instances graded partially labeled. Ambiguous instances are excluded, and simulated and hand-drawn instances appear in one training variant only.
- **Windows:** 300 s, ending on each minute boundary, using only rows at or before the window end. Statistics per sensor are mean, spread, slope, and fraction missing.
- **Splits:** by well. One fold of wells is the holdout. Four development folds compare methods, each setting its threshold on separate validation wells.
- **Operating point:** every threshold sits within 0.05 false alarms per hour and 5% of normal time in alarm on validation wells.
- **Events:** detected only when an alarm episode starts inside the labeled event. Chance level is what unrelated alarms at the measured rate would catch.

# Spatial association: proximity, not attribution

Generated by `pipelines/inspection/reports.py`. Rules: `config/inspection/gate6_association.yaml`, version 2.

## What was compared

455 Carbon Mapper methane plume origins against 645 registry gas wells whose coordinates Gate 2 accepts for spatial analysis (681 in the registry; QUARANTINED 1, UNRESOLVED_DATUM 35, USABLE 645).

A plume and a well are linked as `EMISSION_NEAR` when the plume origin lies within 250 m of the well. Every link is `UNVERIFIED`, carries no confidence value, and is DERIVED. The database refuses to mark one verified or to turn it into `SOURCE_ATTRIBUTED_TO`.

**Disclosures:** the distribution of plume-to-well distances and a uniform-box reference were looked at once, during source inspection, before the radius was fixed, so the other radii are reported beside it. The comparison method below (version 2) replaced the uniform-box baseline after technical review, and was chosen and run after the version 1 numbers were known.

## Proximity against a footprint-matched null

A plume can only be detected where Carbon Mapper observed. Scene footprints are far from uniform: the median scene with a plume covers 19% of the study area. So each plume is compared with 200 points drawn uniformly inside **the footprint of the scene that observed it**, clipped to the study area. That holds fixed where, when, and with which instrument the observation was made. 1 of 455 plume origins falls just outside its own quantized footprint and is kept.

Intervals resample the 142 scenes with plumes (2,000 resamples), not individual plumes, because plumes in one scene share conditions.

| Radius | Plumes with a well inside | Matched null | Difference (points) | 95% scene bootstrap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 m | 14.3% | 3.5% | +10.8 | +7.7 to +13.9 |
| 250 m | 34.7% | 17.0% | +17.8 | +12.8 to +22.8 |
| 500 m | 60.4% | 44.8% | +15.6 | +11.1 to +20.5 |
| 1000 m | 74.5% | 72.3% | +2.2 | -2.1 to +6.5 |

**Persistent sources.** The same source can be detected in many scenes. As a sensitivity check, plume origins that chain within 100 m of each other form one location group, and only the earliest plume of each group is kept (147 groups):

| Radius | Plumes with a well inside | Matched null | Difference (points) | 95% scene bootstrap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 m | 21.8% | 3.4% | +18.3 | +11.6 to +25.0 |
| 250 m | 41.5% | 16.8% | +24.7 | +15.7 to +33.3 |
| 500 m | 61.9% | 44.0% | +17.9 | +10.5 to +25.6 |
| 1000 m | 74.8% | 71.3% | +3.5 | -3.5 to +10.6 |

Within 250 m, plume origins lie near a registry gas well more often than matched points from the same scenes: 34.7% against 17.0%, and 41.5% against 16.8% with one plume per location group. At 1 km the intervals include zero.

**What this does and doesn't show.** Within the observed area, detected plumes sit closer to registry gas wells than an arbitrary observed location does. It doesn't show that any well is a source: wells sit on pads beside tanks, compressors, and pipelines that the registry omits, so a plume near a well is equally a plume near that equipment. The scene bootstrap is still optimistic, because location groups are a rough stand-in for sources and single linkage can merge neighbours.

### Geometric reference, not a chance level

For comparison with version 1 only: uniform points over the whole bounding box, including land no scene observed. This is geometry, not a chance level, and it is not used for any conclusion.

| Radius | Plumes | Uniform points over the whole box |
|---|---:|---:|
| 100 m | 14.3% | 3.2% |
| 250 m | 34.7% | 15.9% |
| 500 m | 60.4% | 41.9% |
| 1000 m | 74.5% | 69.5% |

## Why proximity can't name a source

- **Several candidates.** Of the 158 plumes with a well within 250 m, 45 have exactly one candidate, 72 have two to four, and 41 have five or more.
- **An incomplete registry.** The registry holds gas wells only. Oil wells, tank batteries, compressors, flares, and pipelines are absent, so the nearest registered well isn't necessarily the nearest infrastructure. One chip viewed during development shows a tank battery beside the registered pad; the chips have not otherwise been reviewed.
- **Uncertain locations.** Carbon Mapper states that plume representations may not precisely match infrastructure on the ground. OCD describes its well locations as approximate.
- **Wind and time.** A plume origin is an instantaneous estimate from one overpass.

Nearest-link distances among linked plumes, quartiles: 77, 122, 184 m. Links at other radii: 100 m: 141, 500 m: 1534, 1000 m: 4485.

## What this supports

A statement of the form "a plume origin was detected N metres from this registered well, and K other registered wells are also within the radius." Nothing in Gate 6 supports a leak at a well, an emission source, an equipment condition, or any link to AETHER Field.

# Decision engine on the six AETHER field scenarios

Generated by `pipelines/decision/reports.py` from `results/decisions.json`. Everything here is SYNTHETIC: fictional assets, simulated telemetry, and simulated work orders. No equipment is actuated.

## How a recommendation is made

1. The Gate 5 detector (`aether_hist_gradient_boosting`, bundle `2fca62fa8e8c0a21…`) runs on each scenario's telemetry through the streaming engine, as an operator's system would. Each alarm start carries the three sensors furthest from training normal.
2. The rules in `config/decision/gate7_rules.yaml` (version 3) turn an alarm into a recommendation. Inputs are what an operator would know: the alarm, the planned-operations calendar, open inspection requests, and the network's consequence shares. Simulator truth is never an input.
3. The priority score is a sum of named integer terms: 30 for an alarm start, up to 10 for repeats, up to 10 for age, up to 40 for consequence (share of the field's wells flowing through the asset), and 10 for an open inspection request. Bands: P1 from 60, P2 from 40, P3 below. A detector score only gates "an alarm started"; it is never read as a failure probability.
4. Only FIELD_INSPECTION and CHECK_INSTRUMENTATION create work orders. The engine creates; only a maintenance supervisor may approve, reject, or request evidence.

## Results

| Scenario | Category | Alarms | Decided at | Action | Target (score, band) | Outcome against truth |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| AETHER-FAULT-001-NET | PHYSICAL_FAULT | 1 | 2040-01-04 12:00 | FIELD_INSPECTION | GS-A (50, P2) | DISPATCHED_TO_FAULTED_ASSET |
| AETHER-NET-COMM-DROPOUT | COMMUNICATION_FAULT | 0 | — | — | — | No alarm |
| AETHER-NET-COMPRESSOR-DERATE | PHYSICAL_FAULT | 1 | 2040-01-03 00:15 | FIELD_INSPECTION | C-01 (40, P2) | DISPATCHED_TO_FAULTED_ASSET |
| AETHER-NET-NORMAL | NORMAL | 0 | — | — | — | No alarm |
| AETHER-NET-PLANNED-SHUTDOWN | PLANNED_OPERATION | 2 | 2040-01-04 00:10 | NO_ACTION_PLANNED_OPERATION | — (30) | NOT_DISPATCHED |
| AETHER-NET-PLANNED-SHUTDOWN | PLANNED_OPERATION | 2 | 2040-01-04 12:45 | FIELD_INSPECTION | GS-B (57, P2) | DISPATCH_WITHOUT_FAULT |
| AETHER-NET-SENSOR-DRIFT | SENSOR_FAULT | 0 | — | — | — | No alarm |

- **2 of 3 dispatches went to the faulted asset.** The restriction went to GS-A and the compressor derate to C-01.
- **One dispatch was a false alarm, and it scored highest.** In the planned-shutdown scenario the first alarm fell inside the declared shutdown and was suppressed. The second came 45 minutes after the shutdown window ended, as Pad B came back. Nothing in the rules covers a restart transient, so it was dispatched, and its repeated-alarm and age points made it the highest score of the run. The rules were not changed to hide this.
- **The sensor-drift scenario produced no alarm**, so no recommendation exists. Only a scheduled visit could find it.
- **Localization is weak.** The evidence sensors' deviations are small and close together. In the compressor case C-01 ranked second (deviation 0.098, below well A-03 at 0.112), so the correct target came from rules version 3's consequence ordering, not from the evidence. In the restriction case GS-A led clearly (0.32 against 0.14).
- **Approvals were scripted.** Every work order was approved and completed by scripted demonstration actors under a fixed approve-all policy that never reads truth (`config/decision/demo_decisions.yaml`). They are recorded as `SCRIPTED_DEMO`, never as human decisions. A person's decisions go through `pipelines/decision/decide.py`, recorded as `HUMAN`.

The full chain for each recommendation, from source records to outcome, is in the [evidence audit](evidence_audit.md).

## Rule versions

| Version | Change | When |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Committed rules | Before any alarm or recommendation |
| 2 | The data-quality rule named sensor statuses the simulator never emits; it now uses the contract's quality values | Before any alarm or recommendation |
| 3 | A work order targets the candidate with the largest consequence share; code had taken the first evidence sensor's asset | After the scenario alarms were seen, before any recommendation |

# Inspection scheduling: a modeled comparison

> **Modeled scenario estimates for a fictional facility.** Every figure below comes from a simulation of fictional AETHER Field under declared assumptions (`config/decision/economics.yaml`, version 2). None is a realized saving, an expected saving, or a forecast for any real operation.

Generated by `pipelines/decision/reports.py` from `reports/decision/results/economics.json`.

## Setup

- **Horizon and replicates:** 365 days, 200 replicates, seed 20261110. Each replicate draws one year of faults and false alarms; all three strategies face the same draw, so their differences come from scheduling.
- **Assets:** 31 fictional assets at 16 inspection sites (12 well pads, 3 gathering segments, the compressor station), located on the Gate 4 network. Nominal flow through each asset is its median in the Gate 4 normal run.
- **Faults (assumed):** well 0.3, flowline 0.15, gathering_segment 0.2, compressor 0.6 per asset per year; 25% are sensor faults with no production loss. A physical fault defers 20% of the flow through its asset at $2.50 per Mcf until repaired.
- **Detector (measured in Gate 5, held-out regimes):** detection share DERATE 0.88, RESTRICTION 0.56, SENSOR 0.21; delays drawn between the Gate 5 quartiles; 8.0 false alarms a year. Wells and flowlines borrow the restriction results, an assumption, because Gate 5 has no well-specific category. 80% of real-fault alarms are assumed to target the faulted asset.
- **Field work (assumed):** one crew, 10 h a day, 2 h on site, 90% chance an inspection finds a physical fault, 1 day to repair, $120 an hour, $1.20 a km at 30 km/h with a 1.3 road factor.
- **Strategies:** fixed rounds every 30 days in a fixed geographic order; risk-based dispatch on each approved alarm (2 h approval delay), one out-and-back trip each, plus a round every 90 days; route-optimized, the same triggers with each day's alarms and round stops routed together by OR-Tools (261 distinct tours solved in the main run).

## Results

Mean per year, with the 5th to 95th percentile across replicates for the total.

| Strategy | Total | Labor | Travel | Deferred production | Site visits | Alarm trips | Trips finding nothing | Days to repair |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fixed rounds | $285,201 ($111,939 to $591,115) | $51,949 | $609 | $232,643 | 208 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 18.8 |
| Risk-based | $386,676 ($88,030 to $988,091) | $23,256 | $336 | $363,084 | 92 | 12.6 | 9.3 | 30.2 |
| Route-optimized | $386,652 ($88,030 to $988,073) | $23,237 | $331 | $363,084 | 92 | 12.6 | 9.3 | 30.2 |

Paired differences, replicate by replicate:

| Comparison | Mean | 5th to 95th percentile | Replicates cheaper |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Risk-based minus fixed | $101,475 | −$151,393 to $516,185 | 32% |
| Route-optimized minus fixed | $101,451 | −$151,424 to $516,182 | 32% |
| Route-optimized minus risk-based | −$24 | −$86 to −$1 | 100% |

**Under these assumptions, fixed monthly rounds cost least on average.** Risk-based dispatch saves labor, but with the selected detector catching about half of restrictions, stretching rounds to 90 days leaves physical faults running longer, and deferred production dominates the cost. The spread is wide because a single fault on the trunk segment can dominate a year. **Route optimization changes almost nothing**: the field is about 4 km across and a day holds four or five stops, so there is little travel to save.

## Sensitivity

Each assumption scaled by ×0.5 and ×2 with everything else fixed. Probabilities are capped at 1.

| Assumption | Factor | Fixed | Risk-based | Route-optimized | Cheapest |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `fault_rate_per_asset_year` | ×0.5 | $157,609 | $192,327 | $192,302 | Fixed rounds |
| `fault_rate_per_asset_year` | ×2 | $504,485 | $707,198 | $707,431 | Fixed rounds |
| `production.deferred_share_while_faulted` | ×0.5 | $168,879 | $205,134 | $205,110 | Fixed rounds |
| `production.deferred_share_while_faulted` | ×2 | $517,844 | $749,760 | $749,736 | Fixed rounds |
| `production.gas_price_per_mcf` | ×0.5 | $168,879 | $205,134 | $205,110 | Fixed rounds |
| `production.gas_price_per_mcf` | ×2 | $517,844 | $749,760 | $749,736 | Fixed rounds |
| `travel.cost_per_km` | ×0.5 | $284,897 | $386,508 | $386,486 | Fixed rounds |
| `travel.cost_per_km` | ×2 | $285,810 | $387,012 | $386,982 | Fixed rounds |
| `labor.cost_per_hour` | ×0.5 | $259,226 | $375,048 | $375,033 | Fixed rounds |
| `labor.cost_per_hour` | ×2 | $337,150 | $409,932 | $409,889 | Fixed rounds |
| `inspection.finds_physical_fault` | ×0.5 | $640,466 | $968,452 | $968,427 | Fixed rounds |
| `inspection.finds_physical_fault` | ×2 | $254,900 | $328,631 | $328,607 | Fixed rounds |

Fixed rounds stay cheapest on average under every single change tried. That is a statement about these assumptions together, not about inspection strategy in general.

## Limitations

1. Every rate, cost, and probability is assumed for a fictional field. Only the detector's behaviour and the network's flows come from earlier gates, and both are themselves synthetic.
2. A dispatch that finds nothing produces no second alarm in this model, although a real detector would keep alarming on a persisting fault. That favours fixed rounds.
3. Detection delays are drawn between Gate 5 quartiles, and Gate 5's held-out regimes are themselves a small synthetic benchmark.
4. A strategy mixing alarm dispatch with monthly rounds wasn't declared before the run, so it isn't reported.
5. Crew capacity, travel, and repair are simplified: one crew, straight-line distances with a road factor, and repairs that always succeed once a fault is found.

# D1 final result: gathering-line restriction diagnosis

**Outcome: NOT MET.** One preregistered in-regime line failed: measurement top-1 gain was 0.008 (interval 0.000 to 0.023), against at least 0.08. Every other in-regime line passed. Three of six held-out regimes also failed lines, though they don't change the outcome label. Nothing was tuned, changed, or rerun after the final cases were generated.

Date: 2026-11-11. Preregistration version 4. Frozen method `fb38a97`, freeze record `5d0b018`, run from a clean `main` at `bda4a9d`. Attempt ledger: [`final/attempts.jsonl`](final/attempts.jsonl). Outcome: [`final/outcome-final_in_regime-score-001-final_held_out-score-001.json`](final/outcome-final_in_regime-score-001-final_held_out-score-001.json).

> Everything here is SYNTHETIC: fictional AETHER Field and its uncalibrated Gate 4 network model. The in-regime cases come from the same model the method inverts (an "inverse crime"), so in-regime scores mainly test the implementation. The held-out regimes are the meaningful test. Nothing here is evidence about a real gathering system.

## Execution

| Attempt | Status | Cases | Refused by simulator | Diagnosis failures |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `final_in_regime-generate-001` | Completed | 150 | 0 | — |
| `final_held_out-generate-001` | Completed | 240 (6 × 40) | 0 | — |
| `final_in_regime-score-001` | Completed | 150 | — | 0 |
| `final_held_out-score-001` | Completed | 240 | — | 0 |

Each split was generated once and scored once. A first launch command never started Python, because quoting joined each module name to its argument. It left no ledger entry and no file, and the four attempts above followed it.

## In-regime acceptance (150 cases: 128 restriction, 22 no restriction)

Support met: 128 primary cases (minimum 90), 22 no-restriction (minimum 15), and 63 cases with impact at least 0.1% of field flow (minimum 40).

| Line | Value | Rule | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top-1 | 0.992 | ≥ 0.70 | PASS |
| Top-1 beats B1 | difference 0.33 to 0.50 (B1 top-1 0.578) | lower end > 0 | PASS |
| Top-3 | 1.000 | ≥ 0.90 | PASS |
| Specificity | 1.000 | ≥ 0.80 | PASS |
| Miss rate | 0.008 | ≤ 0.10 | PASS |
| Joint success | 0.992 | ≥ 0.55 | PASS |
| Impact within tolerance | 1.000 | ≥ 0.80 | PASS |
| Median relative impact error | 0.004 | ≤ 0.15 | PASS |
| Brier skill against climatology | 0.971 | ≥ 0.50 | PASS |
| Expected calibration error | 0.044 | ≤ 0.10 | PASS |
| 80% coverage, severity / impact | 0.859 / 0.836 | 0.72 to 0.88 | PASS |
| 95% coverage, severity / impact | 0.977 / 0.969 | 0.90 to 0.98 | PASS |
| Measurement entropy reduction | 0.284 | ≥ 0.25 | PASS |
| **Measurement top-1 gain** | **0.008 (0.000 to 0.023)** | **≥ 0.08, lower end > 0** | **FAIL** |
| Measurement against random | 0.019 to 0.076 | lower end > 0 | PASS |

The failed line is the one review expected. Top-1 was already 0.992 before any measurement, so it could rise by at most 0.008, which it did. Measurement entropy reduction, which failed on development data (0.19), passed here (0.28).

Burden, recommended against random: 130 portable DP and 20 shut-in tests against a uniform mix; mean duration 1.13 h against 1.85 h; 13% against 25% production-interrupting. The recommended action also beat a random action of the same type (interval 0.0005 to 0.056).

Per-pipe results (support at least 8): every reported in-regime pipe had top-1 of 1.0, except FL-A-04 at 0.9 (10 cases). FL-A-05 had 7 cases and is INCONCLUSIVE. FL-A-06, FL-B-03, and GS-TRUNK have no in-regime cases, by design.

## Held-out regimes (240 cases, 34 restriction and 6 no-restriction in each)

| Regime | Top-1 (≥ 0.55) | 80% coverage, severity / impact (0.65 to 0.92) | Joint success | Specificity | B1 top-1 | Lines |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Severity high | 1.000 | **0.529 / 0.500** | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | coverage FAIL |
| Unseen pipes | 0.971 | 0.735 / 0.706 | 0.971 | 1.000 | 0.824 | PASS |
| Noise high | 1.000 | 0.824 / 0.853 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.676 | PASS |
| Deliverability outside | 0.971 | 0.824 / 0.853 | 0.971 | 1.000 | 0.324 | PASS |
| Compressor outside | 1.000 | 0.882 / **0.029** | 0.500 | 1.000 | 0.647 | impact coverage FAIL |
| Degraded operations | **0.412** | **0.441 / 0.588** | 0.382 | 1.000 | 0.059 | top-1 and coverage FAIL |
| **Pooled** | **0.892** (204 cases, ≥ 0.60) | | | | | PASS |

The unseen-pipes regime scored a Brier skill of 0.953 against the fixed in-regime climatology, and 0.934 against its own generator frequencies.

What failed, examined after the fact without changing anything:

- **Degraded operations: the method can't localize where it has no data.** When the faulted pipe was on the pad whose telemetry was lost before diagnosis, it was ranked first in 3 of 22 cases. When the fault was on the other pad, it was ranked first in 11 of 11 cases. Two cases where the faulted flowline's own well was shut in were both missed.
  - **The pipe ranking mostly signalled its uncertainty.** In 12 of the 20 misses, the top pipe got 0.3 or less, with probability spread across the dropped pad's indistinguishable candidates. In 7, it got between 0.3 and 0.9, mostly favouring "no restriction". One miss was confidently wrong: case 002 gave 0.99998 to FL-A-01 when the fault was in GS-A. Correct answers got 0.82 on average.
  - **The severity and impact intervals didn't widen** with the missing data. Their 80% coverage was 0.44 and 0.59.
  - This is the most important finding. The case-by-case evidence is in [`final/degraded_operations_audit.json`](final/degraded_operations_audit.json), extracted read-only from the results file whose SHA-256 the attempt ledger records.
- **Compressor outside the trained range: localization holds, impact doesn't.** Every faulted pipe was ranked first, but impact was overestimated by a median factor of 1.6 (range 0.18 to 2.7), so impact coverage was 0.03. With a unit offline and the setpoint outside the trained range, the station's response no longer matches the method's assumption that all compressors are available at the measured suction pressure.
- **Severity high: accurate, but overconfident.** The severity mean absolute error was 0.0001, while the median 80% interval was only 0.0005 wide, so the intervals missed the truth about half the time. Accuracy isn't the problem here; the uncertainty is understated at the top of the severity range.

Three regimes passed outright: unseen pipes, high noise, and deliverability outside the training range. The method localized pipes it never saw restricted in development (top-1 0.971), and it ranked no-restriction cases first in every regime.

## What this shows and doesn't

- Inside the model it was built on, inverse diagnosis localizes and sizes restrictions almost perfectly, with calibrated uncertainty. It beats the residual baseline by 33 to 50 points of top-1, and it recommends measurements that are more informative and less burdensome than random ones.
- It does not yet earn the measurement step: when the diagnosis is already certain, no measurement can improve it, and the preregistered gain wasn't reached.
- It is brittle exactly where real fields are hard: missing telemetry, equipment states outside its assumptions, and extreme severities. There its intervals don't widen as its accuracy falls, although its pipe ranking mostly does show the uncertainty when telemetry is missing.
- None of this is evidence about a real field. The cases are synthetic, the model is uncalibrated, and in-regime cases share the method's model structure.

## Disclosures

- Before the final run, the preregistration went through versions 1 to 4 and the freeze through three records, every change timed before any final result. See the [D1 specification](../../docs/product/d1_diagnostic_spec.md) and [development report](development_report.md).
- One final held-out case's parameters were built in memory before the final freeze, while checking the degraded-operations fix. No telemetry or truth was produced.
- The degraded-operations timing was set after the first freeze and before any final case.
- Per-case rows are kept in `data/gold/diagnostics/results/`, which isn't committed. Metrics and acceptance lines are in `final/`.
- **Correction after review.** The first version of this report said the degraded-operations "probabilities and intervals stay confident instead of widening". The audit extract, produced after review from the recorded results and changing nothing, shows that was wrong about the pipe probabilities, which mostly did spread out. It was right about the intervals. The wording above was corrected. No number, line, or outcome changed.
